All four cheap gates confirmed by running them. Here is the evidence-based report.

---

# Verification gate feasibility — `zimmermann-pwa`

Branch: `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`. I ran gates 1-4; `git status --porcelain` was byte-identical before and after all four runs (29 entries, unchanged) — **none of them writes to the repo.**

## Gate summary table

| # | Gate | Command | Runs today? | Wall time | Writes repo? | Exit code at baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Typecheck | `npx tsc --noEmit` | YES | **15.1s** | No | 0 (clean) |
| 2 | Unit | `npx vitest run` | YES | **15.1s** | No | 0 |
| 3 | Lint | `npm run lint` | YES | **14.6s** | No | **1** (17 errors) |
| 4 | Token audit | `npm run audit:tokens` | YES | **0.43s** | No | **1** (19 unacked) |
| 5 | Storybook G4 | see below | YES, with caveats | ~2-4 min cold | **Yes — `storybook-static/`** (gitignored) | unknown, never run locally |
| 7 | Playwright | `npx playwright test` | NO | — | `playwright-report/`, `test-results/` (gitignored) | blocked |

Caveat on timings: I ran 1+4 concurrently and 2+3 concurrently, so 2 and 3 may be ~1-2s inflated by CPU contention. Sequential figures will be at or below these.

---

## 1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — CONFIRMED 0 errors

```
npx tsc --noEmit  4.69s user 0.86s system 36% cpu 15.130 total
```
No diagnostic output at all. Clean. `--noEmit` writes nothing (no `incremental`/`tsBuildInfoFile` in play). **Best first gate — fastest signal of a real break.**

## 2. `npx vitest run` — CONFIRMED 354 / 22

```
 Test Files  22 passed (22)
      Tests  354 passed (354)
   Duration  12.29s
npx vitest run  17.58s user 7.59s system 166% cpu 15.082 total
```

**Subset running: yes, and it matters a lot.** Two mechanisms, very different cost:

- **Path filter (fast — use this).** `npx vitest run overrides/app/pages/product-detail` → `1 passed (1) / 15 tests`, **1.84s total**. Only collects matching files. ~8x faster than the full run.
- **`-t` name filter (slow — avoid).** `npx vitest run -t "richText"` → `1 passed | 21 skipped (22)`, **4.45s**. It still transforms and collects all 22 files before skipping, so you pay most of the collection cost.

Config confirms the include glob and that an empty selection won't fail the loop — `vitest.config.ts`:
```
include: ['overrides/**/*.test.ts', 'overrides/**/*.test.tsx'],
passWithNoTests: true,
```
Note `passWithNoTests: true` is a **loop hazard**: a typo'd path filter exits 0 with zero tests run. Assert on the reported test count, not just the exit code.

Two pre-existing stderr lines (`Could not parse CSS stylesheet` from `overrides/app/theme/index.test.tsx`) are noise on a passing suite — don't let the loop treat stderr as failure.

## 3. `npm run lint` — CONFIRMED 17 errors / 16 warnings. **`lint:fix` EXISTS.**

```
✖ 33 problems (17 errors, 16 warnings)
  17 errors and 0 warnings potentially fixable with the `--fix` option.
npm run lint  7.23s user 1.09s system 57% cpu 14.593 total
```
Exit code 1. All 17 errors are `prettier/prettier` formatting; the 16 warnings are `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` and `restrict-template-expressions`.

### Answer to your critical question — three separate facts, all confirmed in source

**(a) `pwa-kit-dev lint` does accept `--fix`.** `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/bin/pwa-kit-dev.js` lines 428-437:
```js
program
    .command('lint')
    .description('lint all source files')
    .argument('<path>', 'path or glob to lint')
    .option('--fix', 'Try and fix errors (default: false)')
    .action(async (path, {fix}) => {
        const eslint = p.join(require.resolve('eslint'), '..', '..', '..', '.bin', 'eslint')
        execSync(
            `${eslint} --resolve-plugins-relative-to ${pkgRoot}${fix ? ' --fix' : ''} "${path}"`
        )
    })
```

**(b) The npm script does pass through extra args**, and a `lint:fix` script already exists in `package.json`:
```json
"lint": "pwa-kit-dev lint \"overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}\"",
"lint:fix": "npm run lint -- --fix",
```

**(c) Plain `npm run lint` does NOT auto-fix.** Verified empirically — `git status --porcelain` was unchanged after the run, and the failure message echoes the exact resolved command with no `--fix` present:
```
error: Command failed: /Users/.../node_modules/.bin/eslint --resolve-plugins-relative-to /Users/.../node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev "overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}"
```

**Loop implication.** `npm run lint` is safe and non-mutating. But because `lint` forwards `--`-args verbatim into a shell `execSync`, **any agent that appends args to `npm run lint` can silently turn it into a writer.** Pin the loop to the literal string `npm run lint` with no argument interpolation, and treat both `npm run lint:fix` and `pwa-kit-dev format` (`prettier --write`) as forbidden in the verify phase.

Also worth knowing: there is **no changed-files-scoped lint**. The glob `overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}` is hardcoded in the script, so lint is always whole-project (~14s). You can bypass npm and scope it yourself:
`node_modules/.bin/eslint --resolve-plugins-relative-to node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev "overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**/*.tsx"`

## 4. `npm run audit:tokens` — CONFIRMED 19 / 16, writes nothing

```
19 unacknowledged violation(s) found.
npm run audit:tokens  0.10s user 0.05s system 34% cpu 0.429 total
audit:tokens exit=1
```
`"audit:tokens": "node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs"`. Grepping the script for `writeFile|writeFileSync|mkdir|createWriteStream|appendFile|rm(|unlink` returns **zero matches** — it is read-only by construction, confirmed by unchanged `git status`. Sub-second, so run it on every iteration.

Baseline detail for delta comparison: of the 19 unacknowledged, 6 are in `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` (lines 722, 723, 724, 775, 833 and one above the window I captured), 2 in `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts`, 1 in `overrides/app/theme/components/navConstants.ts`. The 16 acknowledged are all in footer / zimmButton / zimmLogo / zimmNavItem / zimmTextInput / zimmSubscribe* / footerShared.

---

## 5. Storybook G4 gate — runnable, and the `http-server` blocker is **not** actually a blocker here

The exact CI step, `.github/workflows/qa.yml` lines 258-265:
```yaml
      - name: Run Storybook interaction and a11y tests
        run: |
          npx http-server storybook-static --port 6006 --silent &
          npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 60000
          node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006
```

### Binary availability

| Binary | Status |
|---|---|
| `node_modules/.bin/test-storybook` | **EXISTS** (`@storybook/test-runner@^0.24.4`, devDep) |
| `node_modules/.bin/wait-on` | **EXISTS** (also `wait-port`) |
| `http-server` in `package.json` | **ABSENT** — `grep -n "http-server\|serve\|sirv" package.json` → no match in any dependency block |
| `node_modules/http-server/` | **ABSENT** |
| global `http-server` | **ABSENT** (`npm ls -g`: only `@angular/cli`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`, `corepack`, `newman`, `npm`, `nx`) |
| **npx cache** | **PRESENT** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.npm/_npx/e5196fa6dc3cecbc/node_modules/http-server` v14.1.1, with a working `node_modules/.bin/http-server` symlink, cached Aug 21 |

So `npx http-server` **works on this machine right now, offline**, resolving from the npx cache — but that is machine-local state, not repo state. It will fail on a clean checkout / fresh CI-like container without network. Treat it as a soft dependency.

### Alternatives already available (no install)

- **`python3 -m http.server 6006 --directory storybook-static`** — `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`, Python 3.14.6. **Zero-dependency, fully offline, most robust choice for the loop.** (`--directory` avoids any `cd`.)
- **`node_modules/.bin/vite`** exists (`vite` via `@vitejs/plugin-react`), so `npx vite preview --outDir storybook-static --port 6006` is technically possible, but `vite preview` expects a Vite build manifest and this Storybook is **webpack5**-built (`@storybook/react-webpack5`), so it is a poor fit — not recommended.
- **`sirv` is present but unusable as a CLI.** `node_modules/sirv@2.0.4` exists as a transitive dep of `storybook`, `vite`, `webpack-bundle-analyzer` — but its `package.json` `files` is `["build.*", "sirv.d.ts"]`, there is **no bin**, no `node_modules/.bin/sirv`, and **`sirv-cli` is not installed**. Library only.
- `serve` — not installed, not in `node_modules`, not global.
- No Storybook flag serves a pre-built `storybook-static` directory. `storybook dev` builds from source; there is no `storybook preview`/`storybook serve` subcommand.

### Best option: skip the static build entirely

`test-storybook --help` shows:
```
  --url <url>       Define the URL to run tests in. Useful for
                    custom Storybook URLs (default: "http://127.0.0.1:6006")
```
The **default URL is already `http://127.0.0.1:6006`**, and `package.json` has:
```json
"storybook": "storybook dev -p 6006",
"build-storybook": "storybook build",
```
`storybook dev -p 6006` serves on exactly that port. So the loop can run:

```
npm run storybook &            # dev server on 6006
npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 120000
node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci
```

This needs **no `http-server`, no `build-storybook`, and writes nothing to `storybook-static/`**. It also gives you incremental webpack rebuilds between loop iterations instead of a full cold build each time — a large win for an iterative loop. Downside: it's a long-lived background process the loop must own and reap, and dev-mode HMR state can drift.

Other useful `test-storybook` flags for a loop: `--includeTags`/`--excludeTags`/`--skipTags` (scope to a subset of stories), `--listTests` (dry-run enumeration), `--maxWorkers`, `--testTimeout`, `--json --outputFile` (machine-readable results — note `--outputFile` **writes**), `--shard`. There is **no path/file filter**, so scoping is tag-based only, and no tags are currently set on any story.

### Story count the gate would run: **100 stories across 22 files**

Two independent counts agree exactly:
- `grep -c "^export const" overrides/**/*.stories.tsx` summed → **100**, across **22** `.stories.tsx` files. Every export name is a story name (`Default` x21, `Inverse` x4, `Absent` x3, …) — no `meta`/helper exports polluting the count.
- The existing `storybook-static/index.json` (built Aug 24 17:28) reports **101 entries: 100 `type: "story"` + 1 `type: "docs"`, 22 unique titles.**

`.storybook/main.js` glob confirms all of them are picked up: `stories: ['../overrides/**/*.stories.@(js|jsx|ts|tsx|mdx)']`.

## Recommended loop gate ladder

```
1.  npx tsc --noEmit                                 # 15s   — hard fail, 0 errors
2.  npx vitest run <changed-dir>                     # ~2s   — fast inner loop
3.  npx vitest run                                   # 15s   — full, before commit
4.  npm run lint                                     # 15s   — compare to 17/16 baseline
5.  npm run audit:tokens                             # 0.4s  — compare to 19/16 baseline
6.  storybook dev + test-storybook --ci              # ~2min — outer loop only
```
Gates 1-5 are ~45s total, fully offline, zero repo writes — a solid unattended inner loop. Gate 6 is the outermost ring. Playwright is out of scope for an unattended loop entirely.

Two things to hard-code as guardrails: **never** append args to `npm run lint` (see §3c), and gates 3/4 exit **non-zero at a healthy baseline** — the loop must diff counts (`17 errors, 16 warnings`, `19 unacknowledged`) rather than assert exit 0.
